samples.author: Compiled by Abu Muhammad Yusuf ibn Zabn Allah al-Utayr
samples.scope: The five tawaf guidance points on source page 8. Qur'an references are made explicit beside the English meanings.
samples.imageAlt: The Ka'bah and pilgrims in the courtyard of al-Masjid al-Haram.
samples.imageCaption: The Ka'bah. Tawaf begins and ends in line with the Black Stone.
samples.reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Pilgrimage, hadith 1218, as cited by the publication.

sections.title: Begin at the Black Stone
sections.english: Begin tawaf in line with the Black Stone, keeping the Ka'bah on your left. Touch the Black Stone or gesture towards it with your right hand, saying: “Allah is greatest.”

sections.title: Idtiba': uncovering the right shoulder
sections.english: For men, uncover the right shoulder throughout the circuits of the Umrah tawaf only.

sections.title: Ramal: walking briskly
sections.english: Men, but not women, walk briskly with short steps during the first three circuits.

sections.title: Between the two corners
sections.english: Between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone, it is Sunnah to say the following supplication:

sections.title: The two rak'ahs after tawaf
sections.english: After completing seven circuits, pray two rak'ahs behind the Station of Ibrahim, reciting Surah al-Kafirun and Surah al-Ikhlas.
sections.note: The book identifies these surahs by their opening words. The paired quotations below reproduce those opening verses, not the complete surahs.

sections.title: A report from Aishah
sections.english: Urwah narrated from Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) that whenever the Prophet ﷺ went to bed at night, he brought his palms together, blew lightly into them and recited Surah al-Ikhlas, Surah al-Falaq and Surah an-Nas. He then wiped as much of his body as he could with his hands, beginning with his head, his face and the front of his body. He did this three times.
sections.note: The source identifies the three surahs by their opening words. These paired verses identify the surahs; they are not a substitute for reciting the complete surahs.
sections.repetition: Three times, as stated in the report.
